Surgical effort may still play a significant role in quaternary cytoreductive surgery (QCS) in ovarian cancer. While advancements in chemotherapy and treatment options have improved outcomes for patients with this disease, QCS remains an essential component of the care plan.

Optimal QCS involves a multi-disciplinary approach that combines surgical expertise with medical oncology's knowledge of chemotherapy regimens and potential side effects. The goal is to achieve maximal therapeutic effect while minimizing complications and improving survival rates.

Research has shown that even in highly advanced settings, such as third-line ovarian cancer (EOC relapse), optimal QCS can significantly prolong survival in selected patients. This suggests that a well-executed surgical intervention can be an important factor in achieving better outcomes for these patients.

Therefore, while technology and chemotherapy have improved the treatment of ovarian cancer, the importance of surgical effort should not be underestimated. A thoughtful and individualized approach to QCS is crucial to delivering optimal care and improving patient outcomes.

It's essential to note that this answer emphasizes the significance of a comprehensive approach to QCS, which includes medical oncology expertise, chemotherapy management, and surgical precision. Effective communication between healthcare providers and patients is also vital in ensuring that each patient receives the best possible care.
